title: DiffLens language analyzer output, protocol version 1
description: Every language analyzer is an executable invoked as `<analyzer> analyze --dir <source tree>` that prints exactly one JSON document matching this schema on stdout and exits 0. It analyses one side (one commit's source tree) of a review; the core runs it on both sides and works out what changed by itself. Logs go to stderr. A non-zero exit means the analysis failed and stderr explains why. The analyzer must not write inside --dir and must not need network access beyond what the language's own toolchain does to resolve dependencies.

language.description: Language id in lowercase, the same ids the core uses for project detection, such as "go".

functions.description: Every function, method and closure worth showing that is defined in the source tree (not in dependencies). Generated files may be included and are flagged.

calls.description: Call sites inside the functions listed above. A callee outside the source tree (standard library, dependencies) is listed in `externals` instead of `functions`.

externals.description: Callees defined outside the source tree that are called from it, so the graph can show them as boundary nodes.

diagnostics.description: Problems that did not stop the analysis, such as a package that failed to type-check. Shown to the user as they are.

id.description: Stable identity of the function across commits: the same function in the old and the new side must get the same id even if it moved within its file or its body changed. For Go: the import path, the receiver type if any, and the name, such as "example.com/payments/internal/refund.(*Service).Request". Closures append their position among the enclosing function's closures, such as "...Request$1".

qualifiedName.description: Name a developer would recognise, such as "refund.Service.Request".

container.description: Package, module or namespace, such as "internal/refund".

test.description: Defined in test code by the language's own convention (for Go: a _test.go file), including helpers and closures there, not only test entry points.

complexity.description: Cyclomatic complexity of the body, 1 for a body with no branches. Omitted when the analyzer cannot compute it.

entryPoints.description: Ways this function is reached from outside the program. Empty or omitted when it is not an entry point.

label.description: What a developer would call it, such as "POST /refunds", "payment.settled" or "payctl refund".

file.description: Where it is registered, if that is not the function itself.

line.description: Line of the call site in the caller's file.

kind.description: always: reached on every path through the caller that returns normally. conditional: reached only on some paths. async: started without waiting for it (a goroutine, a callback registered for later, a message sent).

resolution.description: static: the callee is known from the code. dynamic: an interface or function-value call, resolved to every possible target; each target gets its own call entry.

relation.description: call: the caller invokes the callee. registration: the caller hands the callee to a mechanism the analyzer recognises, which will invoke it later (an HTTP route, a middleware, a message handler, a CLI command); `evidence` says which. reference: the caller passes the callee as a value (an argument, a field, a variable) with no known meaning; it may or may not be invoked. For registration and reference, `kind` is "async" and `resolution` is "static".

evidence.description: For registration: what the registration is, as a developer would read it, such as "route POST /refunds" or "middleware". Omitted otherwise.
